title: Course Schedule II
statement: There are numCourses courses labeled 0 to numCourses - 1. Given prerequisites[i] = [ai, bi] meaning bi must be taken before ai, return any valid course order. If no valid order exists, return an empty array.

examples.explanation: The mutual dependency is a cycle, so no order works.

hints: Model bi -> ai edges and count in-degrees, like Course Schedule I.
Repeatedly emit zero-in-degree courses and decrement their neighbors.
If fewer than numCourses courses are emitted, a cycle exists: return [].

solutions.title: DFS Postorder Build
solutions.complexity: Time: O(V + E) | Space: O(V + E)

solutions.title: Kahn BFS Ordering
solutions.complexity: Time: O(V + E) | Space: O(V + E)

editorial.approach: Model courses and prerequisites as a directed graph where an edge u -> v means course u must be completed before v. Compute the in-degree of every vertex and initialize a queue with all nodes having in-degree 0. Repeatedly dequeue a course, append it to the topological order list, and decrement the in-degree of its outgoing neighbours, pushing newly zero-degree nodes into the queue.
editorial.why_optimal: Kahn's algorithm processes every vertex and directed edge exactly once in O(V + E) time and O(V + E) space, producing a valid linear execution sequence if and only if no directed cycle exists.
editorial.pitfalls: Returning a partial list when a cycle prevents completing all courses instead of returning an empty list []. Misorienting prerequisite edges (e.g. treating [a, b] as a -> b instead of b -> a).
